# Lumen Apeiron

> An open-source WebGPU studio for creating IFS fractal flames in a web browser.
> Shape them live, animate them, make them react to sound, breed new forms, and
> share the result. The full name is Lumen Apeiron — The Chaos Master. It runs
> entirely on the visitor's own GPU; there is no account and nothing to install.
> AGPL-3.0.

Lumen Apeiron is a single-page application at https://lumenapeiron.com. It is
JavaScript and WebGPU and will not run in a fetcher, so this file is where a
crawler can learn what it does. Prose about the product lives on the project
site at https://about.lumenapeiron.com.

It needs a WebGPU-capable browser — Chrome or Edge 113+, or Safari 17+ — and a
GPU. Where WebGPU is unavailable the editor does not start.

Following the llms.txt convention documented at https://llmstxt.org.

## What you can make

- **Live 2D and 3D flames** — transforms, variations, symmetry, palettes, colour
  and cameras around a real-time WebGPU render.
- **Fractal foundations** — exact Sierpinski, Koch, Barnsley, Heighway, Cantor
  and Menger constructions, opened as editable flame descriptors.
- **Generative discoveries** — a curated live Home to explore, then randomize,
  mutate, blend and morph any flame into your own.
- **Evolving families** — breed flames, run populations, compare structural
  differences, and trace ancestry.
- **Animation and motion** — keyframe render, camera, transform, variation and
  colour across a timeline, dope sheet and curves, with loops and video export.
- **Sound in both directions** — map music or a live microphone onto flame
  parameters, or turn a flame's structure into sound.
- **Your own mathematics** — author custom variations in WGSL or plain maths,
  with built-in documentation, and create or import palettes.
- **Portable work** — local recents, unlimited undo and redo, import of common
  flame formats, and PNG export that carries the editable flame state inside
  the image.
- **Tools for exploration** — guided tours, share links, a logo and favicon
  generator, and a dedicated Benchmark Studio at
  https://lumenapeiron.com/benchmarks.

## An agent at the controls

Lumen Apeiron registers WebMCP tools on the page, so an agent can read the
flame, run any of the editor's registered commands, and drive the Lumen Arcade
while a person watches. Teach, Cinema and Duel are the Arcade modes with tools
today. Every step is recorded as a replayable lesson, and every write is
validated and guarded.

- [WebMCP documentation](https://github.com/chaos-matters/chaos-master/blob/main/docs/webmcp.md)

  https://github.com/sponsors/chaos-matters

## What Lumen Apeiron is not

Stated plainly because these are the assumptions most often made about
something in this category, and repeating them as fact would mislead someone.

- It is not an image generator and uses no diffusion model or trained network.
  Every frame is the iterated-function-system maths in the descriptor, rendered
  on the GPU.
- It is not a general GPU benchmark. The Benchmark Studio measures this
  renderer's own flame pipeline, and results must come from recorded runs.
- There is no server-side rendering. Execution is local to the browser; a
  separately attested server executor does not exist yet.
- Custom variation code is a bounded, validated TypeGPU-like dialect, not
  arbitrary JavaScript.
- Do not describe it as "formerly Chaos Master". The name is Lumen Apeiron;
  `chaos-master` survives only as the repository and worker identifier.
